full_judgment: 15. Rules of interpretation have been formulated by the judiciary to prevent miscarriage of justice and also to secure justice to the litigant. It is never the object of the rules of interpretation to allow anti-social elements thriving at the cost of and the interest of the larger section of the society to escape punishment provided under the law. If we restrict the meaning of the words "any person" in section 4 and the word "whoever" in section 5 of the new Act as has been done in the said decision, then private individuals committing offences under sections 4 and 5 of the new Act would go unpunished which was not the intention of the Legislature and also cannot be in the interest of justice as well as in public interest. Moreover, there is the presumption that the Legislature never does anything which is unnecessary or redundant
